items.stimulus: An agronomist marks out two triangular test plots so she can compare the yields of two fertilizer blends. Triangle $PQR$ is similar to triangle $STU$, where $P$, $Q$, and $R$ correspond to $S$, $T$, and $U$, respectively. Each side of triangle $STU$ is 3 times as long as the corresponding side of triangle $PQR$. The measure of angle $Q$ is $64^\circ$.
items.stem: What is the measure of angle $T$?
items.explanation: From the letter order, $Q$ matches $T$. In similar triangles, corresponding angles are equal, and the scale factor of 3 changes only the side lengths. So angle $T$ measures $64^\circ$.

A.why: You found the complement of angle $Q$, $90 - 64 = 26$. Nothing in the question uses a right angle, and corresponding angles are equal, not complementary.

C.why: You found the supplement of angle $Q$, $180 - 64 = 116$. Corresponding angles in similar triangles are equal, not supplementary.

D.why: You multiplied the angle by the scale factor, $64 \times 3 = 192$. A scale factor stretches side lengths but never changes angle measures. Also, no angle in a triangle can be more than $180^\circ$.

items.stimulus: On a regional storm-tracking map, a meteorologist draws triangle $ABC$. Point $D$ lies on $\overline{AB}$ and point $E$ lies on $\overline{AC}$, and $\overline{DE}$ is parallel to $\overline{BC}$. On the map, $AD = 40$ kilometers, $AB = 120$ kilometers, and $DE = 50$ kilometers.
items.stem: What is the length, in kilometers, of $\overline{BC}$?
items.explanation: Because $\overline{DE}$ is parallel to $\overline{BC}$, triangle $ADE$ is similar to triangle $ABC$. Set up small over large on both sides: $\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}$, so $\frac{40}{120} = \frac{50}{BC}$. Cross-multiplying gives $40 \cdot BC = 6{,}000$, so $BC = 150$ kilometers.

A.why: You turned one ratio upside down, writing $\frac{120}{40} = \frac{50}{BC}$, and got $BC = \frac{50}{3}$. Keep both ratios in the same order, small over large.

B.why: You paired $AD$ with $DB = 80$ instead of the whole side $AB$, so you wrote $\frac{40}{80} = \frac{50}{BC}$. The large triangle's side is all of $\overline{AB}$, not just the piece below $D$.

C.why: You added the 80-kilometer difference between $AB$ and $AD$ to $DE$. Similar triangles scale by multiplying, not by adding.
